algorithm: ACT (Action Chunking Transformer) with DinoV2 ViT backbone
hand: Inspire Robots hand (6 actuated DoF, 12 total); Fourier GR-1 embodiment instead uses a 1-DoF parallel-jaw gripper
success_criterion: rubric — Success rate per sub-task (pick/place/insert/fold/extract/pass/place), computed over "5 real-world episodes for each task" (Table 1); staged per-sub-task scoring, no numeric threshold.
headline_metric: success rate per sub-task, H1 Can Sorting, DinoV2 backbone vs. baselines (Table 1)
headline_value: H1 Can Sorting: DinoV2 (ours) Pick 92% / Place 88% vs. ResNet18 74%/58% vs. w/o-Stereo 46%/52% (Table 1, 5 real-world episodes per task)
paper_code_mismatch: The paper's prose states 25k training iterations, lr 5e-5, batch size 45, but the code repo's example training command instead shows 50000 epochs and an explicit kl_weight=10 not mentioned anywhere in the paper text.
note_gaps: One of the two embodiments (Fourier GR-1) uses a 1-DoF parallel-jaw gripper rather than a multi-fingered hand; exact trial counts vary by task (5 real-world episodes/task in general, but 30 sub-task trials specifically for GR-1 Can Sorting), so a single settled real_trials figure could not be extracted.
operator_interface: VR headset (Apple Vision Pro or Meta Quest 3) with active stereo video streamed back from a 2-3 DoF camera gimbal on the robot's neck
retargeting_objective: dex-retargeting keypoint-vector optimisation over five wrist-to-fingertip and two thumb-to-finger vectors, solved with SLSQP, with end-effector position taken relative to the head and orientation absolute
latency: 60 Hz stereo round trip and 60 Hz control
mismatch_review: R3 adversarial review: a behaviour-cloning paper with no reward; the charge compared paper iterations to a README example's epochs
